sourceName: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) — 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight

hazards.title: Space Radiation
hazards.summary: Invisible ionizing radiation outside Earth's protective magnetic field and atmosphere, including high-energy galactic cosmic rays and solar storms (solar particle events and coronal mass ejections).
healthEffects: Altered cognitive function and reduced motor function
mitigations: Solar particle event alerts and shielded storm shelter protocols

hazards.title: Isolation and Confinement
hazards.summary: Behavioral and psychological strain among crew members isolated and confined in small habitats far from Earth for months or years.
healthEffects: Sleep loss and circadian rhythm desynchronization
Mood changes, stress, and behavioral health challenges
Work overload and decreased cognitive performance
mitigations: Daily behavioral health and mood monitoring
Light therapy for circadian alignment and alertness
Workload balancing and crew support tools

hazards.title: Distance from Earth
hazards.summary: Extreme distance from Earth limits real-time medical support, instructions, and resupply, requiring crew self-sufficiency and autonomous health assessment.
healthEffects: Delayed ground medical guidance (up to 20 minutes one-way on Mars missions)
No rapid emergency evacuation or immediate resupply
Higher reliance on crew self-triage for medical events
mitigations: On-board autonomous triage dashboards with plain-language guidance
Clear escalation thresholds for contacting crew medical officer and flight surgeon

hazards.title: Gravity Fields
hazards.summary: Transitioning across weightlessness in transit, partial gravity on the Moon or Mars, and Earth gravity upon return affects bones, muscles, fluids, cardiovascular tone, and balance.
healthEffects: Weight-bearing bone mineral density loss (~1% to 1.5% per month in microgravity)
Upward fluid shift to the head, eye pressure, and vision changes
Cardiovascular deconditioning, lightheadedness, and fainting during gravity transitions
Space motion sickness, balance, and spatial orientation shifts
Increased kidney stone risk from dehydration and bone calcium excretion
mitigations: Daily aerobic and resistive exercise countermeasures
Fluid hydration monitoring and cardiovascular tracking
Post-landing readiness and balance re-adaptation protocols

hazards.title: Hostile/Closed Environments
hazards.summary: Maintaining a safe spacecraft habitat ecosystem requires strict control of temperature, atmospheric pressure, air quality, lighting, noise, and microbial communities.
healthEffects: Elevated stress hormones and altered immune system response
Increased susceptibility to allergies, infections, and person-to-person microbe transfer
Respiratory or thermal strain from cabin air-quality, CO2, pressure, or temperature shifts
mitigations: Continuous monitoring of cabin pressure, temperature, and blood oxygen (SpO2)
Microbial swab tracking and habitat air filtration
Early symptom and body temperature checks
